title: Reduced image closures are groupoids over perfect fields
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $(V,R_1,s_1,t_1,e_1,i_1,c_1)$ and $(V,R_2,s_2,t_2,e_2,i_2,c_2)$ be absolute groupoid schemes [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Let $a:R_1\to R_2$ be a morphism which, together with $\mathrm{id}_V$, commutes with all groupoid operations. Assume $k$ is perfect, meaning that in positive characteristic $p$ the map $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective (every characteristic-zero field is perfect). There is a reduced closed subscheme $j:Z\hookrightarrow R_2$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose underlying subset is $\overline{a(|R_1|)}$. Here the reduced induced structure means that on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq R_2$ its ideal consists of the functions vanishing at every point of that closed subset. The source and target of $R_2$ restricted to $Z$, together with restrictions of the unit, inverse and composition, make $(V,Z)$ a groupoid scheme, and $(\mathrm{id}_V,j)$ commutes with all groupoid operations. This assertion includes $a=\mathrm{id}_{R_2}$: the reduction $(R_2)_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow R_2$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] inherits these groupoid operations. No finite-type, separatedness or quasi-compactness hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Put $C=\overline{a(|R_1|)}\subseteq|R_2|$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] to $X=R_2$ and $T=C$. It gives the reduced closed subscheme $j:Z\hookrightarrow R_2$, its stated affine vanishing ideal, and uniqueness over $R_2$. Set $s=s_2j$ and $t=t_2j$.

We will use cancellation of $j$. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $j$ is locally $\operatorname{Spec}(D/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}D$. If $ju=jv$ for two morphisms $u,v:H\to Z$, their underlying maps agree since $j$ is injective. On inverse images of these affine charts their maps on structure sheaves agree, since a map out of $D/I$ is determined by its composite with the surjection $D\to D/I$. Hence $u=v$. Thus $Z(H)\to R_2(H)$ is injective for every test scheme $H$.

source.place: Tag 04Q8 (lemma-map-groupoids-on-perfect-field-image), final sentence: explicit cancellation for the closed inclusion

proof.text: The unit satisfies $e_2=ae_1$, so its set-theoretic image lies in $C$. The field spectrum $V$ is reduced: a nilpotent field element is zero. The inverse $i_2$ is an involution and hence a homeomorphism, by the groupoid axioms [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Since $i_2a=ai_1$ and $i_1$ is also an involution, $i_2(a(|R_1|))=a(|R_1|)$, and consequently $i_2(C)=C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to $e_2:V\to R_2$ and to $i_2j:Z\to R_2$. This gives $e:V\to Z$ and $i:Z\to Z$ with $je=e_2$ and $ji=i_2j$, uniquely by step 2.

source.place: Tag 04Q8, unit and inverse restrictions; Tag 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction) for the scheme factorizations

proof.text: Let $P=Z\times_{s,V,t}Z$. For any affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}E$ of $Z$, their product over $V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_k E)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], where the $k$-algebra structure on $D$ comes from $s$ and that on $E$ from $t$. Both rings are reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Since $k$ is perfect, [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] makes $D\otimes_kE$ reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], applied with the whole base $V$ as its base open and $U,W$ as the opens of the two factors, each $U\times_VW$ is the open subscheme $\operatorname{pr}_1^{-1}(U)\cap\operatorname{pr}_2^{-1}(W)$ of $P$, so these affine products, over all pairs of affine opens of $Z$, cover $P$. Reducedness is local on open covers (a local ring of $P$ is a localization of a reduced ring $D\otimes_kE$), so $P$ is reduced. This uses no equality between $s$ and $t$, and no finite-type hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 04Q8, first proof paragraph, reducedness of the composable-pair scheme; Algebra Tag 00I4 (lemma-perfect-reduced)

proof.text: Put $T=R_2\times_{s_2,V,t_2}R_2$, $D_1=R_1\times_{s_1,V,t_1}R_1$, $b=a\times_Va:D_1\to T$, and $q=j\times_Vj:P\to T$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-product-image-closure] with $f=a$ considered over $V$ via $s_1,s_2$, and $g=a$ considered over $V$ via $t_1,t_2$. The two reduced image closures are both $Z$ by step 1, so $\overline{b(|D_1|)}=q(|P|)$. The closed subset $c_2^{-1}(C)$ of $|T|$ contains $b(|D_1|)$, because $c_2b=ac_1$. It therefore contains its closure $q(|P|)$. Thus $(c_2q)(|P|)\subseteq C$. Since $P$ is reduced by step 4, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives a morphism $c:P\to Z$ satisfying $jc=c_2q$, uniquely by step 2.

source.place: Tag 04Q7 (lemma-map-groupoids-on-field-image), full composition argument via Varieties Tag 04Q0; Tag 04Q8 and Schemes Tag 0356 to factor the composition

proof.text: For every test scheme $H$, steps 3 and 5 give operations on $V(H),Z(H)$ whose images under the identity on objects and the injection $Z(H)\hookrightarrow R_2(H)$ are exactly the ambient operations. Source and target compatibility, both unit laws, both inverse laws and associativity therefore hold: compose each proposed equality of arrows with $j$, use that equality in $R_2(H)$, and cancel the injection from step 2. All maps are scheme morphisms and hence natural in $H$. This is precisely the absolute groupoid definition [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], and its construction makes $(\mathrm{id}_V,j)$ commute with every operation.

source.place: Tag 04Q8, final sentence, with the groupoid axioms verified by cancellation on all test schemes

proof.text: For $a=\mathrm{id}_{R_2}$ we have $C=|R_2|$. By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], $(R_2)_{\mathrm{red}}\to R_2$ is the reduced closed subscheme with this support. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies it over $R_2$ with the $j$ of step 1, giving the asserted reduction groupoid. Every argument above used only the perfect-field condition, the groupoid equations and the stated general scheme lemmas, so the absence of finiteness or separatedness hypotheses is preserved.
